key_insight: Bayesian model averaging generally improved sleep-scoring accuracy and calibration under distribution shift, with multi-basin methods performing best.
clinical_relevance: The findings suggest potential for more reliable biomedical time-series classification across changing data sources, but do not establish clinical benefit in humans.
method: Used rodent sleep scoring as a biomedical time-series case study.
Compared nine approximate inference methods across two neural network backbones.
Tested robustness to genotype, laboratory, and species shifts.
evidence_signal: Evaluation covered in-distribution data and five out-of-distribution datasets; gains were modest in-distribution and generally larger under shift.
watch_item: Benefits were not universal: Bayesian model averaging did not improve inter-rater disagreement detection.
paper_title: Evaluating Bayesian deep learning for robust biomedical time-series classification under distribution shift: A sleep scoring case study
